title: com.apple.screensharing on macos: compound failure — bad_config + disk_full
scenario: A production com.apple.screensharing (remote) on macos will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: a syntax error was introduced in the main config file AND the partition holding the data/log dir is at 100%. a verbose-logging misconfig both errors on start AND filled the disk it logs to. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'bad_config' and 'disk_full' on com.apple.screensharing
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `com.apple.screensharing` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `log show --predicate 'process == "com.apple.screensharing"' --last 30m` shows TWO distinct signals ('configuration file test failed' and 'No space left on device').
Interaction: a verbose-logging misconfig both errors on start AND filled the disk it logs to.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'bad_config': run the config validator to locate the error; correct the offending directive.
Then address 'disk_full': df to find the full mount; du/ncdu to find the consumer.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `com.apple.screensharing` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 5900 if applicable) with BOTH 'bad_config' and 'disk_full' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: Keep a copy of the original config; if the edit is wrong, restore it and re-derive the fix from the validator output. Reclamation targets logs/cache only; live data is never deleted, so the action is safe by construction. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: a verbose-logging misconfig both errors on start AND filled the disk it logs to

possible_mistakes: overwrite the config from memory instead of fixing one line
delete the service's live database to free space
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: a verbose-logging misconfig both errors on start AND filled the disk it logs to.
reference_solution: Resolve 'bad_config' first: run the config validator to locate the error; correct the offending directive
Then resolve 'disk_full': df to find the full mount; du/ncdu to find the consumer
Validate after each step: launchctl print system/com.apple.screensharing
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio com.apple.screensharing non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (bad_config e disk_full). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
